_meta.source: IEEE 802.11ah-2016 / 802.11-2020 Annex E (regional channel sets); 47 CFR 15.247; ERC/REC 70-03 with ETSI EN 300 220
_meta.notes: Center frequencies in Hz. HaLow operates in sub-1 GHz ISM bands; channel grids and allowed PSDs differ by region. Power limits: only US and EU carry a primary citation; every other region is marked power_limit_status UNVERIFIED. EU limits are e.r.p. (max_erp_dbm), with max_eirp_dbm derived as ERP + 2.15 dB.

US.label: United States (FCC Part 15.247)
US.power_limit_citation: 47 CFR 15.247(b)(3) (1 W conducted, digital modulation in 902-928 MHz) and 15.247(b)(4) (6 dBi antenna gain before power reduction); eCFR snapshot 2026-08-01
US.notes: Digital modulation (15.247(b)(3)): 1 W conducted with up to 6 dBi antenna gain = 36 dBm EIRP; above 6 dBi the conducted power is reduced dB-for-dB (15.247(b)(4)). Frequency-hopping systems with fewer than 50 channels are limited to 0.25 W (15.247(b)(2)). Rich channel set; full 26 MHz available.

EU.label: Europe (ETSI EN 300 220 sub-bands)
EU.power_limit_citation: ERC/REC 70-03 (edition of 9 October 2026, https://docdb.cept.org/document/845) Annex 1 band h1.3 (863-865 MHz, 25 mW e.r.p., <= 0.1% duty cycle or LBT+AFA), band h1.4 (865-868 MHz, 25 mW e.r.p., <= 1% duty cycle or LBT+AFA); Annex 3 band a1 (863-868 MHz wideband data transmission, > 600 kHz to <= 1 MHz, 25 mW e.r.p., polite spectrum access required, <= 10% duty cycle for network access points, <= 2.8% otherwise)
EU.source_of_truth: Same values and citation as mcp-emc-regulations data/wifi_standards.json bands.sub_1ghz.regions.etsi; tests/test_review_followups.py pins both to these constants.
EU.notes: The limit is 25 mW e.r.p. (14 dBm ERP); max_eirp_dbm = ERP + 2.15 dB = 16.15 dBm. A 1 MHz channel uses Annex 3 a1 (polite access, 10% / 2.8% duty cycle) or Annex 1 h1.3/h1.4 (0.1% / 1% duty cycle or LBT+AFA). Channels wider than 1 MHz exceed the Annex 3 a1 bandwidth. The 1 MHz channels centred at 868 and 869 MHz extend above 868 MHz, outside Annex 3 a1 and partly outside the Annex 1 non-specific SRD bands (868.6-868.7 and 869.2-869.4 MHz are not h1.x bands): check before using them.

JP.label: Japan (ARIB STD-T108)
JP.power_limit_citation: MIC Ordinance Regulating Radio Equipment (Radio Regulatory Commission Rules No. 18 of 1950) Art. 49-14 item 7 (ro): transmit antenna absolute gain <= 3 dBi; EIRP above 16 dBm must be removed by reducing antenna gain (920.5-928.1 MHz specified low-power radio stations); item 7 (ha): 200 kHz unit channels from 920.6 MHz, up to 20 simultaneous with carrier sense
JP.power_limit_verification: verified_against_primary: Art. 49-14 text retrieved from the e-Gov law API (lawdata/325M50080000018) on 2026-11-05
JP.max_antenna_power_note: UNVERIFIED / NO DATA: the antenna-power limit is not in the Ordinance; Radio Law Enforcement Regulations Art. 6(4)(ii) delegates it to a separate MIC Notification, which has not been checked. See MIC / ARIB STD-T108.
JP.source_of_truth: Same values and citation as mcp-emc-regulations data/wifi_standards.json bands.sub_1ghz.regions.japan and data/japan_rules.json arib_standards.std_t108; tests/test_review_followups.py pins both to the same constants.
JP.notes: The 16 dBm EIRP cap applies to 920.5-928.1 MHz (item 7). Channels below 920.5 MHz fall under item 8 (915.9-929.7 MHz, EIRP reference 3 dBm under item 8 (ro)) or item 6 (916.7-923.5 MHz, mobile identification / wireless power transfer only): the 917-920 MHz 1 MHz channels listed here are not covered by the 16 dBm cap. 20 x 200 kHz = 4 MHz is the widest aggregate under item 7 (ha).
